summary: This informational RFC describes the role and responsibilities of the Independent Submission Editor (ISE), who approves documents in the Independent Submission stream, working with editors and reviewers and the RFC Production Center. It was replaced by RFC 8730.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6548 describes the Independent Submission Editor, who is responsible for the Independent Submission stream of RFCs. The IAB appoints the editor, who reviews and approves submissions and coordinates their path to publication; RFC 8730 later obsoleted this model.

questions: what does the independent submission editor do
what qualifications are desired for an independent submission editor
subtitle: The role and responsibilities of the Independent Submission Editor.

tldr.problem: The Independent Submission stream needs an editor responsible for reviewing and approving its submissions within the RFC publication model.
tldr.mechanism: The IAB appoints an Independent Submission Editor who oversees the stream, coordinates review and publication, and may establish advisory support.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6548 is Informational and was obsoleted by RFC 8730.

today: RFC 6548 is Informational and was obsoleted by RFC 8730.

sections.title: The Independent Submission Editor
sections.content:
The RFC series has multiple streams that produce draft RFCs. The Independent Submission stream has an Independent Submission Editor (ISE) as its stream approver. The ISE is responsible for the stream and works with draft editors and reviewers, the RFC Production Center and Publisher, the RFC Series Editor, and the IAB.

The ISE and the Independent Submission stream are not under the authority or direction of the RFC Series Editor or the RFC Series Oversight Committee. The ISE is appointed by and responsible directly to the IAB.
sections.plainLanguage: The ISE is responsible for submissions in the Independent Submission stream. The IAB appoints the ISE, who works with reviewers and the publication organizations.

sections.title: Qualifications and Selection
sections.content:
The RFC lists desired qualifications, including broad technical experience, familiarity with the RFC series, the ability to establish review arrangements, good standing in the technical community, editorial skills, and the ability to work in a setting with divided responsibilities. These are desired qualifications, not absolute requirements.

The IAB selects the ISE after collecting input from the community, using an approach similar to its selection of an IAOC member. The ISE role is considered a volunteer function.
sections.plainLanguage: The ISE should understand a wide range of Internet technology and be able to edit technical documents. The IAB selects the person after gathering community input.

sections.title: Responsibilities and Editorial Support
sections.content:
The ISE maintains technical quality, reviews and approves Independent Submissions, forwards approved drafts to the RFC Production Center, develops the scope of the stream, reviews and approves errata, and coordinates with the IAB and RFC Series Editor on series policies. The ISE may select an Advisory Board for special topics.

An Independent Submission Editorial Board supports document review. It is a volunteer board that exists at the ISE's pleasure, and its members serve at the ISE's pleasure.
sections.plainLanguage: The ISE reviews submissions, handles approved drafts and errata, and coordinates policy. A volunteer editorial board can help review documents.

sections.title: Security and Status
sections.content: The RFC says it has no specific security implications beyond the security considerations in the documents it references. It is an informational model for the Independent Submission Editor role.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo describes an editorial role and reports no specific security implications. RFC 8730 later obsoleted it.
